cues: When the main verb is in the past, the verb in the subordinate clause is normally past too.
He said that he was unwell.
They left before the guests arrived.

Three exceptions: a universal truth stays present, he said that honesty is the best policy; a comparison after than may keep its own tense; and a present habit may be kept: she told me that she goes to the gym every morning.
text: The sequence of tenses. When the main verb is in the past, the verb in the subordinate clause is normally past too. He said that he was unwell. She asked what I wanted. They left before the guests arrived. Three exceptions: a universal truth stays present, he said that honesty is the best policy; a comparison after than may keep its own tense; and a present habit may be kept: she told me that she goes to the gym every morning.
